turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
Using the training set, the strongest reproducible motifs for MAPbI₃ p-i-n devices are:

- **ITO/FTO glass substrates** rather than polymer/textile substrates.
- **Fullerene-based ETLs with passivating/blocking interlayers**, especially `PCBM-60 | BCP`, `C60 | BCP`, `PCBM-60 | C60 | BCP`, or `PCBM-60 | Bphen`.
- **Selective HTLs with good band alignment**, especially `PTAA`, doped/modified `NiO-c`, and high-performing polymer HTLs such as `P3CT-Na`.
- **Low-recombination back contacts**, particularly Ag with fullerene/BCP interlayers, Al with PTAA-based stacks, and Cu with PTAA when a good hole-selective layer is present.
- **Spin-coated small-area devices** generally dominate the highest median efficiencies, though some coated variants can still be strong if the stack is very well matched.

The candidates most consistent with the highest training anchors are:

1. **c038** — `SLG | ITO / PCBM-60 | PEI / Au-np | NiO-c / Ag / Spin-coating`  
   This is closest to the very high `PCBM-60 / Au-np | NiO-c / Ag` training motif (~20%). The added PEI can improve electron selectivity/passivation, while NiO-c gives strong hole extraction and band alignment.

2. **c030** — `SLG | ITO / IDTT2FPDI | PCBM-60 | Bphen / PTAA | PMMA / Al / Spin-coating`  
   This closely matches the high `PCBM-60 | Bphen / PTAA | PMMA / Al` training motif (~19.5%). PTAA:PMMA gives good film quality and low interface recombination, while Bphen/IDTT2FPDI/PCBM gives a favorable electron-selective cascade.

3. **c041** — `SLG | FTO / PCBM-60 | BCP / NiMgLiO-c / Ag / Spin-coating`  
   This is a strong analogue of high NiO-based p-i-n stacks such as `PCBM-60 | BCP / NiO-c-based HTL / Ag`. Mg/Li-doped NiO should improve hole transport and selectivity, while BCP passivates the electron-collecting side.

4. **c044** — `SLG | ITO / PCBM-60 | BCP / PTAA / Cu / Spin-coating`  
   PTAA/Cu is a high-performing training cluster, especially when paired with fullerene/BCP ETLs. The stack should have good hole extraction and suppressed interfacial recombination.

5. **c097** — `SLG | ITO / ITCPTC-Se | C60 | BCP / P3CT-Na / Ag / Spin-coating`  
   This matches the strong nonfullerene/fullerene-cascade + `P3CT-Na` motif seen near the top of the training data. The C60/BCP electron-selective stack and P3CT-Na HTL give good selectivity and reduced voltage loss.

Final: c038, c030, c041, c044, c097
